scope: Read-only review of appearance.py, workspace_chrome.py, calendar_widgets.py, calendar_list.py, import_dialog.py, and import_preview.py. No production UI changes.

principles.name: Proximity follows meaning
principles.application: Keep period navigation beside the date heading, keep full-day expansion beside the view switcher, and distinguish short gaps inside groups from larger gaps between groups. Preserve these relationships when the toolbar wraps.

principles.name: Consistent visual forms communicate consistent roles
principles.application: Retain segmented controls for mutually exclusive view and series-scope choices. Ordinary actions, toggles, selection, and keyboard focus should remain distinguishable rather than sharing one green treatment.

principles.name: Typography establishes hierarchy without excessive variety
principles.application: Use the desktop font, a small set of roles, and a consistent scaling system. Give the current period and event titles priority; keep times and sync status legible. Review mixed stylesheet pixel sizes and painter point sizes together.

principles.name: Low visual weight must still remain readable
principles.application: Use 4.5:1 as the normal-text contrast benchmark. For essential control/state indicators use the relevant 3:1 non-text benchmark. Decorative calendar gridlines need not all reach 3:1. Server colors should remain available as event accents while text is chosen for legibility.

principles.name: Do not communicate important state through color alone
principles.application: Preserve the source visibility eye icon, a distinct creation-target state, and restrained selected-event borders/bars. Supplement calendar color with source names in tooltips or other existing descriptive contexts.

principles.name: Build on the desktop rather than a second visual platform
principles.application: Keep Qt widgets, native behavior, and inexpensive canvas painting. Prefer a few coherent color and spacing roles over broad custom styling. Treat GNOME guidance as relevant desktop design advice, not a proposal to migrate Qt to GTK.

preserve: Fast native desktop UI and familiar keyboard interactions
Source colors supplied by calendar servers
Separate controls for the creation calendar and calendar visibility
Semantic navigation, view, series-scope, and event-action groups
Mild event selection using weight, border, and a vertical bar
Stable sidebar/search space and navigation geometry
Compact import source field, date selection, and tooltip-only event details

contrast_method.calculation: WCAG sRGB relative luminance; colors taken from code, QColor.darker() evaluated by installed PySide6, event source alpha composited over the weekday canvas before contrast calculation.
contrast_method.caveat: These are code-level sampled states, not a complete accessibility conformance evaluation. Weekend backgrounds, candidate/preview states, rendering, screen scale, and complete keyboard/focus behavior need separate checks. WCAG ratios are used as useful readability benchmarks for this native app.

priority_opportunities: Make hour labels, muted text, event times, and light-source event titles legible before adding visual decoration.
Reduce competition between the large brand and current-period heading; use a restrained, consistent type hierarchy.
Unify margins and group gaps into a small spacing scale while preserving the current toolbar's semantic grouping.
Clarify keyboard focus, chosen segment, source target, and selected-event states with distinct but restrained cues.
Apply the same button, type, spacing, and selection language to import without adding an event-details pane.
